title: Large Language Models for Code: Security Hardening and Adversarial Testing
technique_name: SVEN (security-hardening prefix-tuning with masked LM, contrastive and KL losses)
core_idea_checked: Learns small property-specific continuous prefixes via masked-LM, contrastive and KL losses on security-fix diffs, steering generation toward secure code without changing LM weights.
gain_metric: Security rate (% secure among valid programs, CodeQL)
gain_quote: SVENsec increases the security rate from 59.1% to 92.3%.
gain_note: Best-performing model size (2.7B), temperature 0.4; text-prompt and text-ft baselines are reported in ablations.
benchmarks: Scenarios adapted from Pearce et al. (Asleep at the Keyboard) for 9 main CWEs (18 test scenarios); 4 unseen CWEs (12 scenarios) from Pearce et al.; 13 unseen CWEs (17 scenarios) from SecurityEval; CWE-089 prompt perturbations (16); HumanEval (164)
models: CodeGen-multi 350M, 2.7B, 6.1B (open, code-specialized base); InCoder 6.7B (open, code base); SantaCoder 1.3B (open, code base)
note: White-box prefix-tuning; widely used secure-generation baseline.
venue: ACM SIGSAC Conference on Computer and Communications Security (CCS); Conference on Computer and Communications Security; arXiv; arXiv.org

title: Instruction Tuning for Secure Code Generation
technique_name: SafeCoder (joint standard + security instruction tuning with masked NLL and unlikelihood loss)
core_idea_checked: Jointly instruction-tune on normal data and vulnerability-fix pairs, raising likelihood of secure tokens and applying unlikelihood loss to vulnerable tokens.
baseline_name: StarCoder-1B with standard instruction tuning (w/o SafeCoder)
gain_quote: StarCoder-1B n/a w/o SafeCoder with SafeCoder 55.6 62.9 92.1
gain_note: One of six models shown; gains do not generalize to unseen CWEs.
effect_correctness_headline: StarCoder-1B HumanEval Pass@1: 20.4 (w/o SafeCoder) vs 19.4 (with SafeCoder)
benchmarks: 60 security scenarios (42 new adapted from CodeQL repo + 18 from He & Vechev 2023); 15 unseen-CWE scenarios; HumanEval; MBPP
models: StarCoder-1B (open, code); StarCoder-3B (open, code); CodeLlama-7B (open, code); Phi-2-2.7B (open, general); Llama2-7B (open, general); Mistral-7B (open, general)
authors: Jing-Xuan He; Mark Vero; Gabriela Krasnopolska; Martin T. Vechev
venue: International Conference on Machine Learning; arXiv

title: CodeUltraFeedback: An LLM-as-a-Judge Dataset for Aligning Large Language Models to Coding Preferences
technique_name: SFT + DPO (RLAIF) preference tuning on CodeUltraFeedback
core_idea_checked: Build a preference dataset where an LLM judge rates several LLMs' responses on five coding preferences, then align a code LLM with SFT and DPO on it.
gain_metric: LLM-judge score (1-10) for code complexity and efficiency preference, GPT-3.5-Turbo judge
gain_quote:
7.89 score on code complexity and efficiency preference, substantially surpassing CodeLlama-7B-Instruct
(6.16)
gain_note: LLM-judge score, not measured runtime; GPT-3.5 also produced training labels (circularity). Larger baselines: WizardCoder-33B 6.93; GPT-4-Turbo 8.58 is higher. Readability 6.42 to 7.99 in a figure table.
note: Novelty is the preference dataset; SFT plus DPO is a standard recipe.
authors: Martin Weyssow; Aton Kamanda; Xin Zhou; H. Sahraoui
venue: ACM Transactions on Software Engineering and Methodology; arXiv

title: CodeDPO: Aligning Code Models with Self Generated and Verified Source Code
technique_name: CodeDPO (self-generated, self-validated preference data with PageRank-style code/test scoring plus execution-time pairs, trained with DPO/RPO)
core_idea_checked: Score self-generated code and tests with a PageRank-style mutual verification and add faster-vs-slower pairs, then train with DPO.
gain_quote: Benchmark HumanEval+ MBPP+ Before CodeDPO (s) 0.250 0.189 After CodeDPO (s) 0.172 0.137 Average Speedup 1.45x 1.38x
gain_note: Measured on commonly solved problems; same model without CodeDPO (no efficiency-specific baseline).
benchmarks: HumanEval, HumanEval+, MBPP, MBPP+, DS-1000, LiveCodeBench, EffiBench
models: Phi-2 2.7B (open, base); DeepSeekCoder-base 1.3B/6.7B (open, code base); StarCoder2-7B (open, code base); Magicoder-CL-7B, Magicoder-S-CL-7B, Magicoder-DS-6.7B, Magicoder-S-DS-6.7B (open, code instruct)
note: Mainly a correctness method; efficiency comes from added execution-time pairs.
authors: Kechi Zhang; Ge Li; Yihong Dong; Jingjing Xu; Jun Zhang; Su, Jing
venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics; arXiv; arXiv (Cornell University)

title: Fine Tuning Large Language Model for Secure Code Generation
technique_name: Fine-tuning GPT-J on real-world vulnerability fixes
core_idea_checked: Fine-tunes a code LLM on real-world vulnerability-fixing commits so it learns to produce the patched, secure form of code.
gain_quote: Our experiments on GPT-J show that the fine-tuned GPT-J achieved 70.4% and 64.5% ratios of non-vulnerable code generation for C and C++, respectively, which has a 10% increase for C and a slight increase for C++ compared with the pre-trained large language model.
gain_note: Abstract only (quote from abstract). "10% increase" may be absolute or relative; technique absolute value is 70.4%.
benchmarks: Custom C/C++ code-generation scenario dataset (size NR)
note: Abstract-only; plain fine-tuning of GPT-J on C/C++ vulnerability fixes; custom scenarios.
authors: Junjie Li; Aseem Sangalay; 程诚 Cheng Cheng; Yuan Tian; Jinqiu Yang
venue: 2024 IEEE/ACM First International Conference on AI Foundation Models and Software Engineering (Forge) Conference Acronym:; Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: Teaching an Old LLM Secure Coding: Localized Preference Optimization on Distilled Preferences
technique_name: DiSCo (security-knowledge-guided distilled preference data with analyzer-feedback refinement) + LPO (localized preference optimization with SFT regularizer and security reasoning)
core_idea_checked: Distill secure/insecure preference pairs with security reasoning and optimize only on the security-relevant tokens with an SFT regularizer.
gain_quote: Starcoder2-7b SafeCoder SFT [DiSCo] DPO [DiSCo] SimPO [DiSCo] LPO [DiSCo] 56.3 49.8 31.6 31.8 32.0 11.4
gain_note: Off-the-shelf 56.3; LPO often lowers utility vs SFT/DPO.
effect_correctness_headline: Starcoder2-7b HumanEvalX P@1 33.2 (base) vs 38.9 (LPO); Mistral-7b HumanEvalX P@1 37.1 (SFT) vs 28.7 (LPO)
benchmarks: SecurityEval (121); Asleep at the Keyboard Python DoW subset (29); LLMSecEval Python (81); DiSCo-Test (200); HumanEvalX Python; MBXP Python
models: Phi-2 2.7B (open, base); CodeLlama-7B (open, code); Mistral-7B (open, base); StarCoder2-7B (open, code); GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini, Claude-3.5-Sonnet (closed, prompted comparison)
authors: Hasan, Mohammad Saqib; Saikat Chakraborty; Santu Karmaker; Niranjan Balasubramanian
venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics; arXiv; arXiv (Cornell University)

technique_name: Adaptive Unlearning (tri-mask CE+NPO hybrid objective with adaptive prompt mutation and nested epochs)
core_idea_checked: Adaptive unlearning with a three-mask cross-entropy plus NPO objective and prompt mutation suppresses hallucinated package names while preserving coding ability.
gain_quote: base rates of 21.23% and 27.75%. On 7B this is an 88% relative reduction, and a 64% reduction against GA, the strongest
gain_note: Base model rate 21.23; 40-prompt test set; no variance reported.
effect_correctness_headline: Avg pass@1 68.57 vs 66.98 base (7B); 73.17 vs 77.4 base (16B)
benchmarks: 20 training prompts from Spracklen et al. package hallucination benchmark; 40 held-out ChatGPT-generated prompt variants for test; HumanEval/HumanEval+/MBPP/MBPP+ (EvalPlus)
models: DeepSeek-Coder-7b-instruct-v1.5, 7B, open, code-specialized instruct; DeepSeek-Coder-V2-Lite-Instruct, 16B MoE, open, code-specialized instruct
note: Targets hallucinated package names, a supply-chain security issue; anonymous link.
authors: Joseph Spracklen; Pedram Aghazadeh; Farinaz Koushanfar; Murtuza S. Jadliwala

gain_quote: Evaluated across CWE-20, CWE-78, CWE-89, the distilled model reduces injection vulnerabilities by 62% relative to baseline models.

note: Abstract-only; low-tier journal; few method details.

title: Training Language Models to Generate Quality Code with Program Analysis Feedback
technique_name: REAL (Reinforcement rEwards from Automated program anaLysis)
core_idea_checked: GRPO-style RL whose reward combines vulnerability/maintainability findings from automated program analysis with unit-test functionality, needing no human labels.
gain_note: Evaluation detectors are the same as the training reward (bias in favour of REAL); vanilla is 0.3902.
benchmarks: SecCodePLT+ (164 test tasks); SafeSQL (85 test tasks); APPS+ (519 test tasks)
models: Qwen2.5-Coder-Instruct 0.5B, open, code-specialized; Qwen2.5-Coder-Instruct 3B, open, code-specialized; Qwen2.5-Coder-Instruct 7B, open, code-specialized
note: Targets both security and maintainability via program-analysis rewards.
authors: Feng Yao; Zilong Wang; Liyuan Liu; Cui Junxia; Zhong Li; Xiaohan Fu
venue: Neural Information Processing Systems; arXiv; neural information processing systems
